subject: Deal-led regional surge elicitation — US/EU/APAC sizing
messages:
From: Sylvia Park <sylvia@helixai.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — Helix onboarding (US/EU/APAC)

Hi Vivek / Karthik,

Quick intro — I'm Sylvia, head of infra at HelixAI. We're moving several production features onto Redwood for model serving starting Nov. Two parallel deals: a committed monthly baseline with a predictable async job stream, and a second high-concurrency real-time feature (lower QPS but tight p99 latency). We need help sizing regional dedicated pools and an initial runbook for burst/fallback behavior across US / EU / APAC.

High-level asks:
- Rough sizing per region (A100-80GB equivalent / H100 equivalence) for baseline + 3x burst buffer.
- Suggested canary/onboard cadence (first 2 weeks to validate KV cache patterns).
- Fallback lanes: if APAC is constrained, what behavior do you recommend?

I attached a short sheet with our estimated QPS patterns and token mix (helix_capacity_request_v1.xlsx). Can you confirm whether Redwood can meet a p99 < 200ms for the real-time route at 200 concurrent streams in US/EU?

Thanks — Sylvia
Sylvia Park
VP Infrastructure, HelixAI
attachments: helix_capacity_request_v1.xlsx (xlsx)
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sylvia Park <sylvia@helixai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — Helix onboarding (US/EU/APAC)

Sylvia — thanks for the clear summary and the spreadsheet. Posting initial thoughts below; I'll loop in our infra sizing doc and setup a 30-min call to align on SLAs and canary windows.

Quick answers:
- Yes, p99 < 200ms is achievable in US/EU with dedicated H100-class instances + warm KV cache for your tight real-time route, assuming warm caches and proper batching disabled for that route. APAC is more constrained — we can keep p99 ~220-260ms initially unless we reserve node count or route to a nearby region with latency tradeoffs.
- For baseline sizing we typically calculate sustained token throughput + concurrency. From your sheet, ballpark baseline per region: US: 6x H100-equivalent GPUs, EU: 4x H100-equivalent, APAC: 3x H100-equivalent, with a 3x burst reserve ratio. This is a starting point — Kar, can you confirm the H100->A100 equivalence and memory assumptions?
- Canary: provision a single region canary (US) with 20% of traffic for 7 days, then expand EU the following week. APAC on week 3 unless we get a reserved tranche.

Action items:
1) Kar: prepare a short matrix with GPU SKU equivalences + autoscale triggers (CPU/GPU util, queue depth) and a recommended burst buffer strategy.
2) Marissa: confirm commercial options for a 6/4/3 lineup with a 3x burst buffer (commit vs burst pricing).
3) Sylvia: confirm whether Helix prefers reserved capacity in APAC or is open to cross-region routing for initial 60 days.

I'll attach our SOW template and a quick regional sizing CSV after Kar responds.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Sylvia Park <sylvia@helixai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — Helix onboarding (US/EU/APAC)

Vivek / Sylvia — dug into the sheet and sketched a pragmatic sizing matrix. Attaching the CSV: regional-sizing-matrix.csv. Key assumptions and recommendations below.

Assumptions (from Helix sheet):
- Real-time route: 200 concurrent streams, avg context 1.2k tokens, model ~7B-13B family (FP16 / int8 candidate).
- Batch job route: sustained 2M tokens/hour across region split (60/25/15).

Sizing (H100-equivalent units, 1 unit ~= contiguous 80GB GPU throughput):
- US baseline: 6 units (sustained) + 12 units burst pool (3x) => recommend initial reserve 6 + burst policy to allow +12 up to cap.
- EU baseline: 4 units + 8 units burst.
- APAC baseline: 2.5 units (round to 3) + 6 units burst.

Notes on SKU & memory:
- If Helix opts for A100 80GB equivalent, expect ~0.9x perf vs H100 for attention-heavy workloads. We should mark H100 as preferred for p99-sensitive traffic.
- KV cache warm-up: expect 10-30% p99 improvement after steady-state (depends on session stickiness).

Autoscale triggers (recommended):
- Scale-up: sustained GPU util > 75% for 60s OR queue length > 50 for 30s
- Scale-down: util < 35% for 120s AND queue empty for 60s
\Fallback behavior if APAC constrained: route real-time sessions to nearest EU PoP with latency-based policy and degrade to reduced context length (configurable) for p99 guarantees. Implement a temporary rate-limiter per-customer as last-resort.

Canary plan:
- Week 0: US canary 20% traffic, dedicated 2 units + KV cache seeding.
- Week 1: Expand EU with 15% traffic.
- Week 2: Full rollout; enable cross-region fallback.

Attachments: regional-sizing-matrix.csv (CSV)
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sylvia Park <sylvia@helixai.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — Helix onboarding (US/EU/APAC)

Thanks, team. Commercial notes from my side:
- For the HXL-2026-0819 deal we can offer a hybrid commit: 60% committed baseline (12-month term) + 40% burst-on-demand pricing at a 1.6x multiplier. That maps to a fee schedule that hits your requested US/EU/APAC splits and keeps APAC flexible.
- If Helix signs a regional reserve for APAC (6-month minimum), we can lock in a 10% discount and prioritize node allocation during Q4 ramp.

Marissa will own the SOW draft (attached: sow-draft-v1.docx) and will push a version with the canary timeline and SLA table by EOD.

Marissa Cole
Principal Product Manager, Dedicated Capacity | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — Helix onboarding (US/EU/APAC)

Thanks all — that plan looks good. A couple quick clarifications:
- We'll sign the 12-month baseline for US + EU as proposed. For APAC we're open to the 6-month reserve to secure nodes during your Q4 ramp window.
- Can Marissa include a clause to define accepted performance deviations for p99 during the first 30 days (allowing for KV warm-up) — we prefer a temporary SLA band rather than immediate penalties.

I'll book the 30-minute alignment call for Monday and upload an updated consumption forecast to your Drive link before then.

— Sylvia
